title: Roles Activity Annotator & Rollback UX - compact timeline for org/workspace permission changes
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Design a compact, scannable UI component — the Roles Activity Annotator — that surfaces permission changes across orgs and workspaces, explains who made the change, why (PR/approval link), a concise access-impact summary, and a one-click rollback or mitigation path.

Context: Customers running Redwood Private and Dedicated ask for faster root-cause and remediation for permission regressions and emergency rollbacks without leaving the Console. Existing audit views are verbose and require filter gymnastics; this design aims to be the lightweight first-stop: a timeline scrubber + expandable annotations with cost and rollout context.

Scope:
- Compact timeline across time range selector (last 24h, 7d, 90d) showing grouped change events (role grant, role revoke, permission scope change, role assignment to service principal).
- Each event row shows actor, timestamp, workspace/org scope, affected principals count, quick-sentiment indicator (safe | risky | unknown) derived from risk rules.
- Clicking an annotation expands an inline panel with: change diff, links to justification or ticket (Confluence/Drive/GH), approval chain, estimated request-rate/cost impact (delta tokens-per-minute estimate), and a suggested rollback or compensating action.
- Rollback flow: contextual modal that pre-populates the prior role state, highlights canary rollback suggestion, lists downstream dependencies (list pulled from dependency graph), and shows expected SLO/cost delta after rollback.
- Signed audit artifact generation: ability to export a verifiable snapshot (PDF + JSON hash) for compliance.
- Console integrations: link-to-rollouts to show if change was part of an A/B rollout, and tie into Cost Breakdown dashboard to show token-cost impact of privileged-role actions (e.g., bulk model calls from new service account).

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Keep timeline compact by default (one-line-per-event) and defer verbose diffs to the inline expansion. Trade-off: initial scannability vs quick access to full context. We chose scannability to reduce cognitive load for incident responders.
- Risk indicator is conservative and surfaced prominently; accuracy depends on upstream rule tuning. We include an explicit "why flagged" tooltip to avoid trust issues.
- Rollback affordance will be gated by RBAC: not all users see rollback CTA; the UI surfaces required approvers and next steps if user lacks permission.

Accessibility and performance:
- Timeline uses semantic list elements and respects reduced-motion prefs for scrubber animations.
- Color-coding uses three-way patterns + iconography for color-blind friendliness.
- Designed for keyboard-first navigation and screen-reader labels for each event and inline panel.

Prototype & artifacts:
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/REDACTED/roles-activity-annotator (working prototype v1.3)
- Confluence brief: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Roles+Activity+Annotator+PRD
- Design spec: drive.google.com/drive/folders/REDACTED/annotator-specs
- Example export artifact (mock): drive.google.com/file/d/REDACTED/audit-snapshot.pdf

Open questions:
- Backend: what guarantees do we have for generating prior-state snapshots? (Action: Eng to confirm retention window and shape of stored diffs; see ENG-41290)
- Cost estimate model: use simplified token-rate heuristic or integrate with Optimize predictions? (Decision pending tradeoff meeting 2026-03-05)
- Rollback safety: should rollback be a suggested playbook or an atomic operation? Legal/compliance prefers auditable steps; Product prefers fast undo. Interim: implement canary rollback with mandatory approver for org-scoped actions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Figma prototype with interactive scrubber and expansion panels approved by PM and Eng (done)
- Accessibility checklist passed for keyboard and screen-reader flows (in progress)
- Design handoff includes annotated component tokens and state diagrams for engineering
- Security review run and sign-off recorded in Confluence

Next steps:

- Add explicit API surface doc with required endpoints for diffs and rollback orchestration (owner: Eng infra)
- Prepare a usability session with three customer SREs (scheduled 2026-03-16)
